positions.name: SpectrographCalibrationVerified
positions.frame: Is the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration figure presented as a bare specification, or as a verified, settled state grounded in reference evidence?
positions.why: All three expressions converge on the same directional read: the 88.4 MHz figure is not offered as a raw spec but as something checked against the June reference plates and holding across the band. src-1 performs this as a settled narrative claim ('is now calibrated ... We verified ... it holds'), while src-2 and src-3 restate the identical content in flat field-label form ('**Instrument**:', '**Calibration**: ... verified against June reference plates') — the matter-of-fact/technical register and expert, evidence-grounded power reading are shared across all three. There is a mild conviction gradient worth holding in tension: src-1 reads as a performed decision (the settling itself), while src-2 and src-3 read as plain claims restating that settling in cataloguing form — same content, different commitment texture, not resolved here.
